plan.title: Muscle treated vs control DE via limma-trend + pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The expression matrix (12000 genes x 12 samples) was delivered as core-facility-normalized log2(TPM+1) values, not raw counts — the caveat is explicit in the data profile. Count-based negative-binomial tools (DESeq2/edgeR/pyDESeq2) assume raw integer counts and cannot be validly applied to already-log2-transformed, normalized data; feeding this matrix into them would misspecify the variance model. The correct approach for pre-summarized log-scale intensity data is limma's linear-model + empirical-Bayes framework applied directly to the log2 values (limma-trend, trend=TRUE), which fits the mean-variance relationship empirically rather than assuming a count distribution (Ritchie et al. 2015, Nucleic Acids Research; robust moderation per Phipson et al. 2016 to guard against hypervariable genes at n=6/group). The plan starts with a QC/exploratory step to confirm sample-metadata alignment (6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch), check per-sample distributions for latent normalization artifacts, run PCA/clustering to detect outliers or unexpected structure, and determine the gene identifier scheme used in the matrix (symbol/Ensembl/Entrez) since downstream enrichment tools require HGNC symbols. The DE step fits ~condition in limma and extracts moderated-t/logFC/BH-adjusted-p results for all genes. A visualization step renders the standard volcano/heatmap views of that result. Finally, an enrichment step interprets the gene list functionally against the WikiPathways human and MSigDB Hallmark human gene set collections staged in this environment, using both over-representation (significant genes) and pre-ranked GSEA (full ranked list) to capture both threshold and sub-threshold signal. No translational/PK/safety/immune elements are added since the research question is a plain DE contrast with no drug, clinical-outcome, or immune-composition angle stated.
